The numbers 1, 2, ..., 2100 are written on a board. Every second, Mark takes two numbers on the board, \( a \) and \( b \), erases them, and replaces them with \( \gcd(a, b) \) and \( \operatorname{lcm}(a, b) \). Mark stops once any move he makes will not change the numbers written on the board. Compute the number of divisors of the 2026th smallest positive integer written on the board when he finishes.

Put your final answer within \boxed{}.

Let \(N=2100\). We sort the board entries with repetitions counted.

For a prime \(p\), a move replacing \(a,b\) by \(\gcd(a,b),\operatorname{lcm}(a,b)\) replaces the two \(p\)-adic exponents
\[
v_p(a),v_p(b)
\]
by
\[
\min(v_p(a),v_p(b)),\ \max(v_p(a),v_p(b)).
\]
So for every prime \(p\), the multiset of \(p\)-adic exponents on the board is invariant.

At the finish, no move changes the board. If two numbers \(a,b\) were incomparable under divisibility, then
\[
\gcd(a,b)<\min(a,b)<\max(a,b)<\operatorname{lcm}(a,b),
\]
so the move would change the board. Thus the final numbers form a chain under divisibility:
\[
x_1\mid x_2\mid \cdots \mid x_{2100}.
\]

For each prime \(p\), the exponents
\[
v_p(x_1),v_p(x_2),\dots,v_p(x_{2100})
\]
must be nondecreasing and have the same multiset as the exponents of \(p\) in \(1,2,\dots,2100\). Therefore \(v_p(x_i)\) is the \(i\)-th smallest \(p\)-adic exponent among \(1,2,\dots,2100\).

We need \(i=2026\). There are
\[
2100-2026+1=75
\]
numbers from \(x_{2026}\) through \(x_{2100}\). Hence \(v_p(x_{2026})\) is the largest integer \(m\) such that at least \(75\) of the numbers \(1,2,\dots,2100\) are divisible by \(p^m\). That is,
\[
\left\lfloor \frac{2100}{p^m}\right\rfloor \ge 75.
\]
Since
\[
\frac{2100}{75}=28,
\]
this is equivalent to
\[
p^m\le 28.
\]
Thus
\[
v_p(x_{2026})=\lfloor \log_p 28\rfloor.
\]

Now compute for primes \(p\le 28\):

\[
\begin{array}{c|ccccccccc}
p & 2 & 3 & 5 & 7 & 11 & 13 & 17 & 19 & 23\\
\hline
v_p(x_{2026}) & 4 & 3 & 2 & 1 & 1 & 1 & 1 & 1 & 1
\end{array}
\]

All other primes have exponent \(0\). Therefore the 2026th smallest number is
\[
x_{2026}=2^4\cdot 3^3\cdot 5^2\cdot 7\cdot 11\cdot 13\cdot 17\cdot 19\cdot 23.
\]

Its number of positive divisors is
\[
(4+1)(3+1)(2+1)(1+1)^6
=5\cdot 4\cdot 3\cdot 2^6
=3840.
\]

\[
\boxed{3840}
\]
